rules_tr: K19 (2026-11-13): eski projenin karakter profillerinde başlığı ve konusu belirlenmiş ama yazılmamış 5 kahramanın 4'er yan hikâyesi (Cassian, Corbin, Dorian, Garrick, Rowan). Kural character_stories_part1.json ile aynı: sahiplik + aşama, bölümler sırayla. Part II sırrı çözülmez; Garrick dünya kuralı 11 gereği şansölyenin adını hatırlamaz; Dorian mührün sahibini adlandırmaz. Sahip onayına açık.

parts.title_en: How the Bell Lost Its Tongue
parts.direction_en: The night after the Bell-Widow falls. Cassian sits on the belfry stair with an iron clapper-ring across his knees. Mahmut finds him there.

lines.text_en: You keep that ring cleaner than your sword.
The sword is for Choir Knights. The ring is for me.
Five years ago I climbed this stair in a storm and cut the clapper free. I thought a bell without a tongue could not take anything.
And?
The next night it rang anyway. No rope. No tongue. The villages lost names all the same.
The chapter sent me down to the flooded doors so no one would ask why the warden had climbed. I stayed, because the doors still needed someone.
A man who disobeys a bad order and then guards the door anyway. I know the type.
Then you know it is not a virtue. It is only the next thing to do.

parts.direction_en: At the refuge fire, Aveline and Cassian tally the pilgrims they brought out of the flooded nave of Saint Luthos.

lines.text_en: Forty-one through the nave doors. Mirel wrote every one of them down before we let them go.
Forty-two. The baker's boy went through on my shoulders. Mirel was busy shouting at the water.
You stood in that water for six hours.
The Choir Knights stood in it longer. Someone had to be more stubborn than the dead.
You could have left with the first group. No one would have counted it against you.
The bell would have. It counts what we leave behind.
Then let me count something for once. Forty-two, and the warden.
...Forty-three. Fine. Write it down before I argue.

parts.direction_en: Rain on the road to the Ashen Lord's estate. Mirel walks beside Cassian, who carries the cathedral folio under his tabard.

lines.text_en: Do not carry it like a shield. It is a folio, not a door.
Everything I carry ends up being a door eventually.
If the rain reaches the binding, the names in the seventh gathering run together. I cannot recopy what I cannot read.
Then it rides under my tabard and I walk in the rain. That is the whole plan.
You are very calm for a man carrying the only record of what the chapter took.
I was calm when I cut the clapper too. Calm is only the part people see.
Keep the folio dry, Cassian. I will keep you honest.
That is the better trade for both of us.

parts.direction_en: Below the altar, between two braziers, Cassian scratches a name into the fuller of his greatsword. Aveline sits down beside him.

lines.text_en: You are scratching again. That blade holds more names than my register.
Your register is ink. Ink can be blotted, or burned, or bought.
Iron has to be ground away. Whoever wants these names gone will have to take the sword from me first.
And when the fuller is full?
Then the flat of the blade. Then the hilt. Then I start on the clapper-ring.
You took the bell's tongue and found it a better use.
I took its tongue. It spoke anyway. So now I stand in front of it, and these stand with me.
Then carve one more. The warden who held the nave.
Not yet. A man does not witness for himself.

parts.direction_en: Water drips through the bricked arch of the lowest cistern. Corbin counts the drops; Odelia watches him count.

lines.text_en: You count the drips. I have watched you do it for an hour.
Seventeen a minute here. Twenty-two at the bricked arch. The water is still pushing against what they built.
Two winters ago the Matron ordered the lowest cistern drained and sealed, so her ledger wing could reach the Glass Bell's wards.
I kept the master sluice-wheel. When they came for it, I tried to flood their conduit instead.
And they threw you in the spillway.
In chains. The river remembers its level, even when they brick the arch. So did I.
Someday you are going to open that arch.
Someday. When opening it drowns the right people.

parts.direction_en: Tilda's clinic, after closing. Corbin sits on the single clean table while Tilda checks old stitches and Iona trims the lantern wick.

lines.text_en: Arm up. Slowly. If you tear my stitches again I am charging you for the thread.
You said that two winters ago.
And you still have not paid.
She pulled you out of the canal by your collar. I held the lantern and read your name until you answered to it.
I remember the voice. Not the words. Only that someone kept saying 'Corbin' as if it mattered.
It did. Names come back when someone keeps them warm.
So I bolted the broken sluice-wheel to my arm and stood at your door. Seemed a fair price for one clean table.
The table is still clean because you are standing at the door. Stay there.

parts.title_en: The Chalk Arrow on the Lock
parts.direction_en: The lower cistern stairs. A faded harbor-knot arrow is chalked on the sluice wall, pointing down. Corbin stops beside it with Odelia.

lines.text_en: Your brother came down these stairs two winters ago. I was the last one outside the Guild to see him.
You never told me.
You never asked, and I did not want to be the one who made it true.
Tomas chalked that harbor-knot arrow on the wall. Pointing down. The Guild sent a boy with a scrub-brush the next morning.
And?
I took the brush and threw it in the canal. Then I stood in front of this wall every morning until they stopped sending boys.
It is still here.
It is still here. Whatever he was pointing at, he wanted someone to follow. I would rather it was you than the Guild.
Then we follow it together.

parts.direction_en: With the Matron gone, Corbin sets his hands on the master sluice-wheel he kept for two winters. Odelia holds the lantern.

lines.text_en: Master wheel. Three turns left, one back, then hold.
And if the arch does not give?
Then the water waits. It has waited two winters. It is better at it than we are.
There. Hear that? The lowest sluice, breathing again.
The glass wards on the ledger wing are going dark.
Washed clean. Whatever the Glass Bell keeps, it will not drink from our cistern anymore.
You once said there is one thing you never say about drowned people.
That the water took them. It is never the water. It is whoever bricks the arch. Today the water gives something back.

parts.direction_en: A candle in the Undercity archive room. Dorian turns a seven-notched brass matrix in his gloved fingers while Clem copies headstone names.

lines.text_en: You hold that thing like it bites.
It does. Only slowly.
On Crownfall night I was twenty, a novice at the chancery table. My work was to heat the wax and keep my mouth shut.
Two orders came down at the end. Gray wax for both. Two initials under the seal of the second. I pressed it myself.
Whose initials?
I cut wax. I did not ask. That was the rule. Someone in a wet cloak carried the second order into the rain, and by morning the Inquisition was gone.
I took one thing with me. Seven notches on the brass. Whoever wants it back will know exactly where to look.
Then I am glad it sits in a coat I can find.

parts.direction_en: A cramped room above Tilda's clinic. A family without coin waits at the door while Dorian warms his seal-iron. Iona keeps them company.

lines.text_en: The family at the door has no copper.
Then they owe me a passable lie. Ask the youngest what the Duke's gate guards smell like.
She says onions.
Perfect. That is worth a whole pass. Onions are the one true thing about every gatehouse.
Ducal travel warrant, eastern toll seal, three names. Clem checked the headstones. These are real grandparents.
If they catch you, these papers hang you.
If they catch these three without papers, the road takes their names. My neck is the cheaper price.
You say everything has a fee.
Everything does. Some fees are paid by the one who charges them.

parts.direction_en: Under the bridge gate, Sable lays two captured orders side by side — Rusk's and Oren's. Dorian bends over the wax.

lines.text_en: Rusk's order. Oren's order. The same gray wax.
The same recipe, too. I mixed it for years. Pine resin, lamp-black, too much chalk.
Look at the rim. Seven notches, the seventh shallower than the rest. That die was cut for the chancery's private hand.
The matrix in your coat has seven notches.
Mine is a cutter's copy. The private die never left its owner. Someone is still pressing it, two years after the chancery fell.
Then the Inquisition did not end on Crownfall night.
Its table did. Its wax did not.
Keep that copy close. If they learn you can read their wax, they will come for the reader before the seal.
Let them come. I have forged worse letters than my own obituary.

parts.direction_en: Dusk at the company's shelter. Clem writes in her grave-book by hand; Dorian sits on the step below her.

lines.text_en: You never asked why I keep the grave-book by hand.
I assumed you distrust printers. Reasonable people do.
A register can be sealed, filed and forgotten. A book in a gravedigger's coat cannot be filed.
And that is why you check my passes against your stones.
Your forgeries are only as good as the names under them. I make sure the names are true.
The chancery taught me that a seal makes a thing true. You taught me it only makes a thing filed.
So which are you now?
A man who carries a seal and trusts a shovel more.
That is the nicest thing anyone has ever said about my shovel.

parts.direction_en: Night patrol along the orchard firebreak outside Oakhaven. The far bell rings once; Garrick checks the watch-glass at his belt. Jori notices.

lines.text_en: You check that watch-glass every time the bell rings.
Habit. Eight years ago a relief order came timed to the minute by a court chronometer. It arrived one hour late.
I held the outer furnace-gate of a keep while a chancellor's household sheltered inside. The gate fell in fire at the sixty-first minute.
Whose household?
I remember the gate. The draft through the breach. A woman and a boy I could not reach. Liora and Aren.
Their names stayed with me. His did not. I have tried. It slides off like water off hot iron.
That is the bell's work.
Maybe. Or maybe a man who schedules lives to the minute does not deserve to be remembered. Either way, I am never late again.

parts.direction_en: Morning after the mercenaries leave Oakhaven. Garrick drills Rikka's kiln militia with spades behind the forge.

lines.text_en: Again? We dug a firebreak yesterday.
Yesterday's break was two spades wide. Fire jumps two spades. Make it four.
Rusk is gone. The orchards are safe.
Rusk was a schedule. Fire is weather. Weather does not care who won.
Load, timber, draft. Take away one and a fire starves. Your kiln crews already know two of those. Learn the third.
The draft. You want the break cut across the wind.
There it is. Now you are a militia instead of a crowd with shovels.
Is that praise, Captain?
It is a schedule. Four spades by dusk.

parts.direction_en: Under the bridge gate, the Crown Guard's siege winches stand in a row. Garrick lays a gauntlet on the nearest drum; Jori kneels beside the pawl.

lines.text_en: These drums carry your mark.
I drew them. Throne wars. The Crown Guard kept the plans after I walked away.
Pin here, pawl there. Pull the pawl and the drum spins free; the whole line drops its load into the river.
You are taking apart your own work.
I built them to break walls with soldiers behind them. They turned them on a bridge full of people walking home.
Then let me take the pawls. My hands are smaller.
Good. A smith who knows where to strike a gate also knows where to save one.
When the drums fall, do not watch them. Watch the far bank. That is who we did it for.

parts.direction_en: The collapsed gallery. Garrick holds a recovered diagram up to the lantern, its margin lined with times written minute by minute. Mahmut waits.

lines.text_en: You have been staring at that page since the gallery came down.
The hand. Times down the margin, minute by minute. I have seen this hand before.
On a relief order, eight years ago. The one that came an hour late.
Then you know who wrote it.
I know the hand. I cannot hold the name. Every time I reach for it there is only the smell of the burning gate.
A name the bell took still belongs to a man who did something. We can follow what he did.
Then I follow it. No more schedules, Mahmut. Not his. Not mine.
We walk when the people ahead of us need us. Not when a clock says.
Spoken like a man who has been late to something too.

parts.direction_en: Evening at the forest wayshrine. Rowan kneels at an alder way-marker with chisel and mallet; Brin holds the brazier for him.

lines.text_en: Lower with the light. There. The second letter of Bram is nearly gone.
My father's name was on this shrine before I could read it.
The bell rang twice last night. Every time it rings, the bark forgets a little. So I remind it.
With a chisel.
With a chisel. If the tree forgets a letter, carve it deeper.
Does it work?
The old keeper says the bark does not keep the name. The hand that comes back to cut it does. So I keep coming back.
Show me how. I would rather be the hand than the one who watches.

parts.direction_en: The flooded steps of Saint Luthos. Rowan fights to keep five braziers lit in the rain while pilgrims wade toward the road. Aveline brings a crate.

lines.text_en: Three braziers dry, two drowning. I need more tallow and less rain.
Sister Thistle sent wax. It is in the crate marked 'not bread'.
That crate has bread in it.
Then the bread is waxy and the wax is crumbly. Use whatever lights.
The pilgrims come down the steps in the dark. If the fire goes out, they stop. If they stop in the water, the Choir Knights...
That is why you are here and not at your shrine. Keep them walking toward the light.
Yes, Sister. I mean, yes, ma'am. I mean...
Rowan. The fire, please.
Fire. Yes. Fire first.

parts.direction_en: A trade at the refuge road: Rowan's tins of shrine beeswax for Thistle's salves. Neither of them is good at haggling.

lines.text_en: Four tins of beeswax for two jars of comfrey salve. That is a very good trade for you.
The shrine bees worked hard this year. The ash keeps the wasps away.
Ash from the bell?
It falls on the hives every time the bell rings. The bees do not mind. The honey tastes of smoke.
Everything here tastes of smoke.
Then everything here is still burning, and burning means someone is keeping warm.
Fine. Two jars, and yarrow for your cut thumb. Do not argue.
I was not going to argue.
You were going to say it was nothing. That is the same thing.

parts.direction_en: After the altar, at the crater rim. Rowan carves oak road-markers, one for every name in the company. Brin stacks the finished ones.

lines.text_en: One marker for every name in the company. Oak, not alder. Oak holds a letter longer.
You have carved forty already.
Forty-one. I put the old keeper on the first one. He never let anyone carve his name. He is not here to stop me.
The crater is quiet tonight.
Quiet is not gone. The road will still forget, slowly. Someone will have to come back with a chisel.
Then teach the next one, the way he taught you.
That is the plan. Deep enough to last until the next hand finds them.
Carve one for yourself, Rowan.
Last. After everyone else is safe on the board.
